mainTopic: נותן טעם לפגם: does a forbidden food that spoils a dish forbid it? The amud covers the מחלוקת between רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון, and whether עולא or רבי יוחנן is right about which case they argue in.
overview: The amud opens at the end of רבי שמעון's proof from the פסוק about נבלה. Meat that is not fit even for a גר is not called נבלה, so a forbidden food that only spoils a dish does not forbid it. The גמרא explains how רבי מאיר reads the same פסוק, and how רבי שמעון answers him. עולא then says the two תנאים argue only when the forbidden food first improved the dish and later spoiled it. If it spoiled the dish from the start, everyone permits it. עולא defends this rule against רב חגא's ברייתא about vinegar in split beans. רבי יוחנן disagrees and says they argue even when the food spoils from the start, and the גמרא leaves the exact scope of his view as תיקו. רב עמרם finds a source about forbidden leaven falling into dough that was already leavened, which seems to support רבי יוחנן. רבי זירא rejects that proof, because dough is different. The גמרא brings a new ברייתא as another proof and begins to raise the same pushback, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's source: unfit meat is not called נבלה
steps.stepSummary: This line finishes רבי שמעון's proof. A carcass that is not fit for a גר to eat is not called נבלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Meat that is not fit for a גר is not called נבלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing רבי שמעון's proof from the פסוק that a forbidden food which has gone bad is no longer treated as forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה says to give a נבלה to a גר so he can eat it. רבי שמעון learns from this that a נבלה only keeps its איסור while it is still fit to eat. So a forbidden food that ruins the taste of a dish has lost its forbidden status and does not forbid the dish.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that died without proper שחיטה, forbidden to eat
Here, a non-Jew living in ארץ ישראל (a גר תושב), to whom a נבלה may be given

steps.whyThisMatters: This פסוק is the source for the whole idea of נותן טעם לפגם being מותר.

phrases.english: [A carcass] that is not fit for a ger
phrases.notes: This finishes a line that started earlier, based on the פסוק in דברים 14:21: 'give it to the גר in your gates, that he may eat it.'

phrases.english: is not called an unslaughtered carcass.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁאֵין רְאוּיָה לְגֵר אֵינָהּ קְרוּיָה נְבֵלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי שמעון's derivation, which began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נבלה unfit for a גר loses the name נבלה. So a forbidden food that only spoils a dish does not forbid it.

steps.title: How רבי מאיר uses the same verse
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says the פסוק only excludes meat that was rancid from the very beginning.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר? That פסוק comes to exclude meat that was rancid from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי מאיר is not moved by רבי שמעון's פסוק. He reads it as covering a different, narrower case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, the פסוק only teaches about meat that was already unfit when the animal died. Meat that was fit at death became a real נבלה, and it stays forbidden even after it rots. So the פסוק does not prove that spoiled forbidden food becomes מותר.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quietly asking: what does רבי מאיר do with this פסוק?

phrases.english: That [verse] is to exclude [meat] rancid from the outset.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers רבי מאיר's other way of reading the פסוק that רבי שמעון used.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the פסוק to a narrower case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seems to prove that any spoiled forbidden food is מותר.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי מאיר, the פסוק only excludes meat that was unfit from the start, before the animal died.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: rancid-from-the-start meat needs no verse
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון answers that meat rancid from the start is just dust. It does not need a פסוק, so the פסוק must be teaching about meat that spoiled later.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון? Meat rancid from the start does not need to be excluded, because it is just dust.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי שמעון's answer to רבי מאיר's reading of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Meat that was never fit to eat is not food at all, so it obviously is not נבלה. A פסוק would be pointless for that case. Therefore the פסוק must be teaching that even meat that later went bad loses the name נבלה.

keyTerms.meaning: An exclusion (a source that leaves something out)

steps.whatToRemember: Both תנאים use the same פסוק. רבי מאיר says it excludes only meat rancid from the start. רבי שמעון says that case needs no פסוק, so the פסוק teaches that later spoiling also removes the איסור.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon: [meat] rancid from the outset
does not need an exclusion,
it is mere dust.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סְרוּחָה מֵעִיקָּרָא לָא צְרִיכָא מִיעוּטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי מאיר's limited reading by showing that his case would need no פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Making the פסוק necessary (a פסוק is not written for the obvious)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe the פסוק only excludes meat rancid from the start, as רבי מאיר says.
steps.terutzMaskana: That case is obvious, since it is just dust. So the פסוק teaches that meat which spoiled later also stops being נבלה.

steps.title: עולא limits the dispute
steps.stepSummary: עולא says רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון only argue when the forbidden food first improved the dish and later spoiled it. If it spoiled the dish from the start, everyone permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: The מחלוקת is when it improved the taste and in the end spoiled it. But if it spoiled the taste from the start, all agree it is מותר.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא sets a boundary on where the מחלוקת between רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two kinds of cases. In one, the forbidden food first helped the flavor and later hurt it. In that case רבי מאיר forbids, because there was a moment of good taste. In the other, the forbidden food hurt the flavor from the very start, and עולא says even רבי מאיר agrees the dish is מותר.
steps.confusionAlert: According to עולא, even רבי מאיר permits a forbidden food that spoiled the dish from the start. רבי מאיר forbids only when the food first improved the dish and later spoiled it, and that is the only case where the two תנאים argue.

phrases.english: Ulla says:
The dispute is where it enhanced and in the end detracted,
but [where] it detracted from the outset
everyone agrees it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא מַחְלוֹקֶת שֶׁהִשְׁבִּיחַ וּלְבַסּוֹף פָּגַם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the sources are explained, עולא defines exactly which case the מחלוקת is about.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מחלוקת is only in a case of 'improved then spoiled.' If the food spoiled the dish from the start, it is מותר according to everyone.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the coming challenge and decides how wide רבי מאיר's איסור really is.

steps.title: רב חגא challenges עולא from wine in lentils
steps.stepSummary: רב חגא brings a ברייתא where wine fell into lentils and vinegar fell into split beans. The תנאים argue there, even though the spoiling began from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חגא challenged עולא: Wine that fell into lentils, and vinegar that fell into split beans, are forbidden, and רבי שמעון permits. But here it spoiled from the start, and they argue!
steps.whatsHappening: רב חגא attacks עולא's limit using a ברייתא where the two sides argue in a 'spoiled from the start' case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine or vinegar makes lentils and beans taste worse right away. Even so, the first opinion forbids and רבי שמעון permits. That means there is a מחלוקת even when the spoiling began from the start, which seems to contradict עולא.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥagga raised an objection to Ulla:
Wine that fell into lentils,
phrases.notes: He means forbidden wine, like יין נסך.

phrases.english: and vinegar that fell into split beans
it is forbidden, and Rabbi Shimon permits.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא הָכָא דִּפְגַם מֵעִיקָּרָא הוּא, וּפְלִיגִי!
phrases.english: But here it is where it detracted from the outset, and they disagree!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges עולא's claim from the step before.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's claim that everyone permits a food that spoiled the dish from the start
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the ברייתא, wine in lentils and vinegar in beans hurt the taste right away, yet the first opinion forbids against רבי שמעון. So there is a מחלוקת even in a 'spoiled from the start' case.

steps.title: עולא defends himself: the vinegar was poured into cold beans and then heated
steps.stepSummary: עולא rejects רב חגא's question. The vinegar fell into cold split beans, which it improves. Only after the beans were heated did it start spoiling them. So this is a case of 'improved first, spoiled later.'
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: חגא doesn't even understand what the חכמים are saying, and he's raising an objection? The case is where the vinegar fell into cold split beans and then they were heated. That counts as improving first and spoiling later, so it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers רב חגא's question from Step 5. He shows that the ברייתא does not really involve food that spoiled the dish from the very start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Vinegar actually makes cold split beans taste better. It only ruins them once they are heated. So the ברייתא fits עולא's rule: the תנאים argue only when the food improved the dish first and spoiled it later.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Here, what case are we dealing with?' This is a standard way of narrowing a source to a specific case
It improved the taste first and spoiled it later

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think vinegar always ruins beans. In cold beans it improves the taste. It only becomes 'spoiling' once the beans are heated. That timing is the whole answer.

phrases.english: Ulla said:
Ḥagga does not even know
what the Sages are saying,
and yet he raises an objection?
Here, what are we dealing with?
For example, where it fell into cold split beans
phrases.notes: 'It' is the forbidden vinegar from the ברייתא in Step 5.

phrases.english: and then he heated them,
it becomes like something that improved the taste and later spoiled it,
and so it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן? כְּגוֹן שֶׁנָּפַל לְתוֹךְ גְּרִיסִין צוֹנְנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב חגא's objection in Step 5
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא): the split beans were cold first and heated later
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב חגא thought the vinegar spoiled the beans from the very start
steps.terutzMaskana: The vinegar first improved the cold beans and only spoiled them after heating, so it fits עולא's rule

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the argument is about food that spoils from the start
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן disagrees with עולא. He says רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון argue even about food that spoiled the dish from the very beginning.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן says: The argument is about forbidden food that spoils the taste from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second opinion that disagrees with עולא's rule from Step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא said everyone permits food that spoils the dish from the start. רבי יוחנן says no: רבי מאיר forbids even that case. So according to רבי יוחנן, רב חגא's ברייתא needs no special explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: Spoils the taste from the very beginning

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan says:
The argument is about something that spoils the taste from the start.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: בְּפוֹגֵם מֵעִיקָּרָא מַחְלוֹקֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an opposing view to עולא's rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון argue even when the forbidden food spoiled the dish from the very beginning

steps.title: How far does רבי יוחנן's view go? Left unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי יוחנן means the argument is only in the 'spoiled from the start' case, with everyone forbidding 'improved then spoiled.' Or does he mean they argue in both cases? No answer is found: תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: Is the argument only about food that spoils from the start, while everyone forbids food that improved first and spoiled later? Or perhaps they argue in both cases? It remains unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about what exactly רבי יוחנן meant, and it ends without an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's words could mean 'only there do they argue.' In that reading, in the 'improved then spoiled' case even רבי שמעון forbids. Or the words could mean 'even there they argue,' so the argument covers both cases. The question stays open (תיקו).

keyTerms.meaning: 'They asked': this opens a real question the scholars were unsure about
Let it stand: the question stays unresolved

phrases.english: They asked:
Is the argument only about something that spoils from the start,
but if it improved first and spoiled later,
everyone agrees it is forbidden?

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִּלְמָא בֵּין בָּזוֹ וּבֵין בָּזוֹ מַחְלוֹקֶת?
phrases.english: Or perhaps they argue both in this case and in that case?
Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the scope of רבי יוחנן's statement in Step 7
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבי יוחנן limit the argument to 'spoiled from the start,' or extend it to 'improved then spoiled' too?

steps.title: רב עמרם wonders why the משנה doesn't teach רבי יוחנן's case
steps.stepSummary: רב עמרם is surprised. If רבי יוחנן is right that the argument covers food that spoils from the start, the משנה should have taught that case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עמרם said: Is it possible that רבי יוחנן's statement is true, and yet it isn't taught in our משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: רב עמרם raises a question that sets up the next move. He expects to find רבי יוחנן's case hinted at somewhere in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב עמרם assumes an important rule like this should appear in the משנה. His question pushes the גמרא to look for a line in the משנה that teaches the 'spoiled from the start' argument.

keyTerms.meaning: It is so / it is true

phrases.english: Rav Amram said:
Is it possible that this statement of Rabbi Yochanan is true,
and yet it is not taught in our Mishnah?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב עַמְרָם: אֶפְשָׁר אִיתָא לְהָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to finding a source in the משנה for רבי יוחנן's view
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where does the משנה teach that the argument covers food that spoils from the start?

steps.title: Rav Amram finds a source about extra leaven in dough
steps.stepSummary: רב עמרם looks into the sources and finds a teaching. Leaven of חולין fully leavened a dough, and then forbidden leaven (תרומה or כלאי הכרם) fell in. The anonymous view forbids the dough, and רבי שמעון permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עמרם went out, looked carefully, and found a teaching. Ordinary leaven fell into dough and had enough strength to leaven it, and it did. Afterward, leaven of תרומה or of כלאי הכרם also fell in, with enough strength to leaven. The dough is forbidden, but רבי שמעון permits it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב עמרם, who was surprised in Step 9, now digs and finds a source that seems to show the argument does cover a case of spoiling from the start. Here he quotes that source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dough was already fully leavened by kosher leaven. So the forbidden leaven that came later could not help it and could only make it too sour. Yet the anonymous view still forbids and רבי שמעון permits, so this looks exactly like the case רבי יוחנן described.

keyTerms.meaning: Leaven: a very sour piece of dough used to make other dough rise
Ordinary, non-holy food that anyone may eat
The portion given to the כהן, which a non-כהן may not eat
Crops planted together with a vineyard, which are forbidden for any benefit

phrases.english: He went out, examined, and found
that it was taught:
Non-sacred leaven
that fell into the dough,
and there is enough in it to leaven, and it did leaven it,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַחַר כָּךְ נָפַל שְׂאוֹר שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה
phrases.english: and afterward leaven of תרומה fell in
or leaven of כלאי הכרם,
and there is enough in it to leaven:
it is forbidden, and רבי שמעון permits it.
phrases.notes: The unnamed first opinion is understood to be רבי מאיר, the other side of the argument.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב עמרם's own surprise from Step 9 by locating a source that seems to teach the 'spoiled from the start' case.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's claim that רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון argue even when the forbidden item spoils from the start.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A teaching about forbidden leaven falling into dough that was already fully leavened by kosher leaven.

steps.title: The point: here it spoiled from the start, and they still argue
steps.stepSummary: רב עמרם draws the conclusion. In this case the forbidden leaven harmed the dough from the very beginning, and still the תנאים argue.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here it is a case where it spoiled from the start, and they argue!
steps.whatsHappening: רב עמרם spells out why the source he found matters. It shows an argument in a case of spoiling from the start, just as רבי יוחנן said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the dough was already leavened, the extra forbidden leaven gave no benefit at all, only harm. If the תנאים still argue here, then their argument is not limited to 'improved first, spoiled later' like עולא said. This supports רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: It spoiled the taste from the very beginning

phrases.english: But here,
it is a case where it spoiled from the start, and they argue!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא הָכָא, דִּפְגַם מֵעִיקָּרָא הוּא, וּפְלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the source quoted in Step 10.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's view that the argument covers 'spoiled from the start.'
steps.raayaSupportSource: The leaven-in-dough teaching from Step 10, where the dough was already leavened, so the forbidden leaven only harmed it.

steps.title: רבי זירא: dough is a special case
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא rejects the proof. Extra leaven is not pure harm for dough, because a very sour dough can be used to leaven many other doughs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: Dough is different, since it is now fit to leaven several other doughs with it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא pushes back on רב עמרם's proof. He says the dough case is not truly 'spoiled from the start.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the extra leaven makes the dough taste worse, it also makes the dough stronger as a starter for leavening other batches. So the forbidden leaven does add something useful. That means the case cannot prove the תנאים argue where the forbidden item only spoils.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different, a special case
To leaven, to make dough rise

steps.confusionAlert: רבי זירא does not deny that the taste got worse. His point is that dough gains another kind of usefulness, so it is not a clean case of pure spoiling.

phrases.english: רבי זירא said:
Dough is different,
since it is fit to leaven with it
several other doughs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from Steps 10-11 by redefining the dough case as not purely spoiled.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from dough. It does not reject רבי יוחנן's view itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the extra leaven only harmed the dough. Really it also improves the dough as a starter for other doughs.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that 'spoiling' must be judged by every use of the food, not only by its taste right now.

steps.title: A new ברייתא about two kinds of leaven in dough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about leaven of תרומה and leaven of חולין falling into dough. It gives three cases: both fell in together, the תרומה fell first, and the חולין fell first. The גמרא will use this as a new attempt to support רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: Leaven of תרומה and of חולין fell into dough, each one strong enough to leaven it, and they leavened it. It is forbidden, and רבי שמעון permits it. If the תרומה fell in first, everyone agrees it is forbidden. If the חולין fell in first and afterward the תרומה or כלאי הכרם fell in, it is forbidden, and רבי שמעון permits it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new 'come and hear' and quotes a ברייתא. This sets up the next move, where the גמרא will try to prove רבי יוחנן's view from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last case, where kosher leaven fell first and forbidden leaven came after, matches the case רבי זירא just rejected. The new details are the case where both fell together and the case where the תרומה fell first, where everyone forbids. The גמרא will look at these details to see if they settle the question.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Leaven of תרומה and of חולין
that fell into the dough,
this one has enough to leaven
and that one has enough to leaven, and they leavened it:
it is forbidden, and רבי שמעון permits it.
If the תרומה fell in first,
everyone agrees it is forbidden.
If the חולין fell in
and afterward the תרומה fell in
or the כלאי הכרם,
it is forbidden, and רבי שמעון permits it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: שְׂאוֹר שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה וְשֶׁל חוּלִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי זירא rejected the first proof, the גמרא brings a new source to try again to support רבי יוחנן.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's claim that the argument covers food that spoils from the start.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about leaven of תרומה and of חולין falling into dough, with three different orders of falling.

steps.title: The ברייתא shows an argument even when the taste was spoiled from the start
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes from the ברייתא that the forbidden leaven harmed the dough from the start, and still the תנאים disagree. This supports רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here is a case where the forbidden leaven spoiled the dough from the very beginning, and still they argue!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is drawing the lesson from the ברייתא it just quoted. Here the forbidden leaven harmed the dough from the start, and the תנאים still argue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא case, the dough was already leavened, so more leaven from תרומה could only hurt its taste. Even so, the תנאים still disagree about whether the dough is forbidden. This seems to prove רבי יוחנן's claim that the argument also covers food that spoils from the start.

keyTerms.meaning: But look, here is... (an opening that points to a proof)
